scenario.name: Apache Tomcat Security & CISA DFIR — Tomcat AJP Ghostcat (CVE-2020-1938) & /manager/text/deploy WAR Forensics
scenario.overview: A Java application building leaves an internal freight elevator door open directly to the public street. An outsider reaches through that freight shaft to read the building staff passcode sheet, uses those passcodes at the package loading dock to upload a disguised web bundle, and triggers freshly compiled control pages inside the workshop. In this scenario (T1190, Apache Tomcat Security & CISA DFIR, Tomcat AJP Ghostcat , CVE-2020-1938 & /manager/text/deploy WAR Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: aJP/1.3 Port 8009, then authenticated WAR Upload via PUT, then jasper JSP Compilation. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering AJP/1.3 Port 8009, then Authenticated WAR Upload via PUT, then Jasper JSP Compilation, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1190 across the documented kill chain.
